Ubiquitous

yoo-BIK-wih-tus -- built on the Latin word for 'everywhere.' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ubiquitous is present, appearing, or found everywhere.

Free public Wi-Fi has become so ubiquitous in the city that almost every cafe offers it.

Worked Example

A single soft-drink brand's logo appears on billboards, vending machines, restaurant menus, and even stadium scoreboards in nearly every country on Earth.

That overwhelming, everywhere-at-once presence is exactly what ubiquitous means. Unlike 'popular,' which just means widely liked, ubiquitous specifically means found absolutely everywhere.

How Ubiquitous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

omnipresent

omnipresent: present everywhere at the same time

pervasive

pervasive: spreading widely throughout an area or group

universal

universal: applicable to or present in all cases

Antonyms

rare

rare: not found in large numbers; uncommon

scarce

scarce: insufficient for the demand; hard to find

How Strong Is It? — pervasive → ubiquitous → omnipresent

pervasive vs. ubiquitous

pervasive vs. ubiquitous: Pervasive is slightly milder than ubiquitous -- pervasive means spreading widely through an area, while ubiquitous implies an even more total, inescapable presence everywhere at once.

omnipresent vs. ubiquitous

omnipresent vs. ubiquitous: Omnipresent can feel even more absolute than ubiquitous: ubiquitous describes something found almost everywhere, while omnipresent suggests being present absolutely everywhere, without exception.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — ubique

root — ubique: everywhere (Latin)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of, having the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin ubique meant 'everywhere.' Ubiquitous, at its root, simply means 'full of everywhere-ness' -- present in every place at once.

Use the root in a new word: ubiquity

Use the root in a new word: ubiquity: The ubiquity of plastic packaging has become a growing environmental concern worldwide.
